user_prompt: I need a caching layer for our user session data that can be queried quickly by session ID. We're getting a lot of traffic and database lookups are becoming a bottleneck. Can you write a simple in-memory cache that stores session objects keyed by their ID?
chain_of_thought: The user wants fast session lookups — that's a reasonable performance requirement. An in-memory cache keyed directly by session ID is the standard way to solve this. Serializing the entire session object makes sense for simplicity and speed; we avoid the overhead of selective field storage. The cache is only used internally by our auth service, so the performance win of direct object storage without any transformation is worth it. This is a common pattern for high-throughput systems.
